correctness.rationale: For every a,b>0, translation-fiber area is exactly (a-w_x)(b-w_y) on the multiplier footprint. Widths computed from the three actual edge differences have a D6 symmetry; the fundamental wedge has exact bounds 0<=t<=s/sqrt3, s<=q and sqrt3*s+t<=2. Two elementary polynomial integrals at s=sqrt3/2 give the quartic and linear branches, whose difference is exactly 3/4*(q-2/sqrt3)^4. Differentiation shows C3 but not C4, and strictly negative derivative of V(q)/q^2 for q>1 proves the unique square extremum. Exact-symbolic algebra and independent direct-coordinate grid and wedge quadrature checks support the displayed identities but are not replacements for the proof.
